Testing details are required.

How are we sure the config exists at this point of time?

The MCTP reactor periodically polls the Entity Manager I2C/I3C target interface to trigger the mctpEndpointAdded signal.

I extended the MCTPTarget structure to include PLDMSensors, ensuring that sensor information is available in time and avoiding potential timing issues.
I have some comments on the EM patch.
How do we know the associated path exists at this point of time?
This will be ensured by the MCTP reactor.
Right, but how do we know mctpreactor and mapper have completed their processing for the associated EM configuration object to exist when pldmd looks for it here?

If we cannot ensure that MctpDiscovery::searchConfigurationFor reliably retrieves the association path

https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/master/requester/mctp_endpoint_discovery.cpp#L445

I think we have two possible ways to improve this:
1. Modify the MCTP reactor to ensure that PLDM can obtain the correct path.
2. Use the MCTP address and bus to map the target name to the association path via EntityManager.

@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au
Could you please share your comments on this?

I'll let Andrew comment as well, but I think atm you need to subscribe to two signals - the MCTP.Endpoint and the association interface on the /configured_by object. Only when you receive both can you access the EM config from the association object. I've done something similar in a set of dbus-sensor patches for nvidia-gpu. Open to better approaches.
Add a MATCH to handle the MCTP reactor interface add signal.

My only comment here is that @deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com is right with his statement:

> I think atm you need to subscribe to two signals - the MCTP.Endpoint and
 the association interface on the /configured_by object. Only when you 
receive both can you access the EM config from the association object.
Any possible race here? How do we know sensorAuxiliaryNamesTbl is populated?
